corrected_value.authors: Roozenbeek, J., Freeman, A. L. J., & van der Linden, S.
corrected_value.title: How accurate are accuracy-nudge interventions? A preregistered direct replication of Pennycook et al. (2020).

decisions.quote:
Our hypotheses attempted to replicate Roozenbeek et al.’s (2021)
ﬁndings. Roozenbeek et al. tested whether prompting people to
think about accuracy reduced their willingness to share misinfor-
mation and/or increased their willingness to share true information
related to COVID-19 generally. They found the accuracy nudge
decreased intentions to share misinformation but did not signiﬁ-
cantly increase intentions to share true information. Our ﬁndings
are in partial agreement with Roozenbeek and colleagues. The
accuracy nudge did not decrease willingness to share false general
COVID-19 information in Kyrgyzstan or the United States. In India,
the accuracy nudge did decrease willingness to share general
COVID-19 misinformation.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work, and an intact primary-source passage is quoted without line-break hyphen repair. The full text explicitly sets out to test whether the findings of Pennycook et al. (2020) or Roozenbeek et al. (2021) replicate across three samples (Kyrgyzstan in Study 1; India and the United States in Study 2), adopts Roozenbeek et al.'s (2021) frequentist and Bayesian one-tailed t-test analytic framework, and directly compares its empirical results against Roozenbeek et al.'s finding that the accuracy nudge decreases willingness to share false COVID-19 headlines without increasing willingness to share true headlines (Table 3, Results, and Discussion). The reference list (lines 1220-1223) and Crossref metadata confirm the identity of Roozenbeek, Freeman, & van der Linden (2021), Psychological Science, 32(7), 1169-1178, DOI 10.1177/09567976211024535. Shipped row 975 represents only Pennycook et al. (2020) (DOI 10.1177/0956797620939054, sibling target_index 0); Roozenbeek et al. (2021) is an independent replication-chain target by different authors reporting a distinct empirical pattern and is absent from all shipped rows.
